audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] says 'he has no percent-HP or true damage to punish your HP bar', 'late' says 'A Shen with no percent-HP and no true damage can't shred your stacked HP bar', and whys[6] says 'an immobile Shen with no percent-HP or true damage to answer'.
audit.why: Twilight Assault: 'Shen recalls his spirit blade to attack with it, dealing damage based on the target's max health.' That is percent max health, scaled off Nasus's own bar — which is the single stat Nasus stacks hardest. The entry's whole late-game thesis is 'my HP bar is too big for him', and it is built on a premise the kit contradicts. Note this is the identical wrong phrase I found in the Sett entry, where it was also false; it reads as templated filler applied without checking the kit.
audit.corrected: Twilight Assault deals damage based on your max health, so stacking HP alone does not make you safe from Shen.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit's Refuge is described only as 'his W blocks your Q-empowered auto' with no explanation of how to play around it.
audit.why: Riot's text is 'Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked.' The block is anchored to the spirit blade's position, not to Shen himself — so the counter is positional. Step off the blade and the attack lands; there is no need to wait out a duration or bait a cast. That is the single most useful piece of tech in this lane and neither layer mentions the spirit blade at all.
audit.corrected: Spirit's Refuge only blocks attacks near his spirit blade — walk off the blade rather than waiting the duration out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Confirmed — no cooldown number appears in either layer, and breakdown.cooldowns lists Shadow Dash twice.
audit.why: Shadow Dash is 18/16/14/12/10 and Spirit's Refuge is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, against Twilight Assault at 8/7.25/6.5/5.75/5. An 18-second taunt at rank 1 is the largest gap Shen ever gives, and it is the concrete answer to 'when do I commit'. Stand United at 200s at rank 1 is likewise unstated despite the entry telling you to respect his map pressure.
audit.corrected: Shadow Dash 18s at rank 1 down to 10s; Spirit's Refuge 16s at rank 1; Stand United 200s at rank 1. Commit in the Shadow Dash gap.

audit.why: content 'mid' claims 'his W can't block your ult's HP-scaling burn'. This checks out and is worth keeping: Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks, while Fury of the Sands 'batters nearby enemies' as ability damage rather than a basic attack. Good existing detail — I kept it and just named the abilities.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ki Barrier is never mentioned, in an entry whose plan is to win prolonged duels.
audit.why: 'After casting a spell, Shen gets a shield. Affecting other champions reduces the cooldown of this effect.' In an extended duel Shen is shielding himself repeatedly off his own rotation, and the shield's cooldown shortens the more he connects with you. That is directly relevant to a grind-him-down win condition, which the entry recommends without accounting for it.
audit.corrected: Ki Barrier shields him off every spell cast, and connecting with you shortens its cooldown — the prolonged duel is not free.

audit.why: I checked whether Nasus can interrupt Stand United, which the kit flags as a channel ('interruptible — any CC cancels it'). He cannot — Wither is a slow and nothing else in his kit applies interrupting CC. Per the relevance rule I wrote nothing about it rather than adding a line about an interaction Nasus cannot execute.

edits.after: Spirit's Refuge blocks your Siphoning Strike outright while Twilight Assault shoves and pokes you off the wave — peak stack denial.

edits.after: Shadow Dash you into bad trades and shove so you miss stacks under tower

edits.before: Shen owns the first three levels and it's all about his W — it hard-blocks your Q-empowered auto, so a fat Siphoning Strike you walked up for just whiffs. His Q-empowered autos out-poke you and let him shove you under tower, which is the worst case: you bleed stacks. Don't throw Q into his W; bait it out or only Q a minion to stack, and accept you're farming defensively. His E-taunt is the trap — never sit in range to get dashed onto and chunked.
edits.after: Shen owns the first three levels and it is all about Spirit's Refuge — it blocks your Siphoning Strike outright, so the fat Q you walked up for just whiffs. Read it positionally: it only blocks attacks near his spirit blade, so step off the blade instead of waiting the duration out. Twilight Assault out-pokes you and shoves you under tower, which is how you bleed stacks. Shadow Dash is the trap at 600 range — never sit in it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay his: he shoves and roams, and Wither alone doesn't flip a tank who isn't trying to kill you. Level 6 is your one real window — Fury of the Sands plus Wither on his attack speed turns a committed all-in your way, since his W can't block your ult's HP-scaling burn and his slowed autos can't out-DPS your lifesteal. Bait his E-taunt, ult, Wither, and grind. Just respect that his global R means he can win the map even while losing the lane, so ping when he backs to roam.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his: he shoves and roams, and Wither alone doesn't flip a tank who isn't trying to kill you. Level 6 is your one real window — Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks, so it does nothing against Fury of the Sands' burn, and a Withered Shen can't out-DPS your lifesteal. Sequence it properly: wait out Shadow Dash, 18s at rank 1, then ult, Wither and grind. Respect that Stand United still wins him the map even while he loses the lane.

edits.before: This is where you reclaim it. A Shen with no percent-HP and no true damage can't shred your stacked HP bar, and Wither shuts off the one thing he does — his attack speed. With two items and a few hundred stacks, you win the prolonged 1v1 every time: Spirit Fire shreds his armor, lifesteal eats his chip, and his only escape is a taunt you can just ult through. Splitpush and force him to answer you 1v1 — that's the lane you win.
edits.after: This is where you reclaim it, with one correction: Twilight Assault deals damage based on your max health, so stacking HP alone never makes you safe from him. Wither still shuts off his attack speed, and with two items and a few hundred stacks you win the prolonged 1v1: Spirit Fire shreds his armor and lifesteal eats his chip. Splitpush and force him to answer you 1v1 — that's the lane you win.

notes: CHART DIVERGENCE, deliberately NOT edited. content win[] is [Shen,Shen,Shen,Shen,Nasus,Skill,Nasus] while full phases[].side is [Shen,Shen,Shen,Shen,Skill,Nasus,Nasus] — cells 4 and 5 are exactly SWAPPED between the two layers. This is the second matchup in my slice (after Sett) where content and full hold different charts, and in both cases the divergence is in the same 4-6 index range, so I think this is a generator bug rather than authoring drift and it is probably present across all 71 entries. I did not force a fix here because, unlike Sett, the content layer's prose is internally consistent with the content layer's chart: whys[4] describes level 6 as Nasus's window and whys[5] describes Shen's first tank item as restoring parity, which is a coherent and defensible read for a matchup Nasus loses at 48.41%. Converging the chart without also rewriting that prose would create a new contradiction, and picking which layer is authoritative is your call, not mine. Recommend you diff win[] against phases[].side across every entry before anything else in this file gets applied. Second note: the 'no percent-HP or true damage' phrase is wrong here and was also wrong in Sett — worth grepping globally, because as boilerplate it will be false for every enemy with a max-health or true-damage component.
